title: [release/11.0] Stop shipping the obsolete Components.AI package
body:
## Description

Remove the obsolete .NET 11 version of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.AI` so it is no longer built and included in every .NET 11 release. `Components.AI` ships from `main` with .NET 12. This removes its .NET 11 source, tests, test apps, solution entries, build and shipping registrations, and unused dependencies without changing `main`.

Keep the empty shipped API baseline unchanged so the removal does not require changes to shared CI policy.

## Customer Impact

Stop publishing the obsolete .NET 11 package with each .NET 11 release. The .NET 12 implementation remains on `main`. This change does not remove previously published packages.

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

The removal is limited to `Components.AI`, its tests and test apps, and AI-only entries in solution, build, shipping, and dependency files. Other Components code and shared CI policy are unchanged.

## Verification

- [ ] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

The targeted Components build passes. Solution and dependency checks confirm that no AI project or package references remain and that all 54 solution filters reference existing projects.

The Components unit suite reports 1,291 passed, 8 skipped, and 2 failed. Both failures also reproduce with identical messages on unchanged `release/11.0` at `6639242ce5709978f7d627c7d61270658f5e07d2`. The failing tests are `PersistentServicesRegistryTest.RestoreStateAsync_RestoresPreviousRegistryWireFormat` and `PersistentServicesRegistryTest.PersistStateAsync_RestoresStateForPersistedRegistrations`.

Manual review of the release package output remains pending.

## Packaging changes reviewed?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No
- [ ] N/A

This intentionally removes `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.AI` from .NET 11 package output. Packaging review remains pending before requesting servicing approval for `11.0-rc2`.
